question: A 67-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of retrosternal chest pressure and shortness of breath for 4 hours. The symptoms started while he was walking to work and have only minimally improved with rest. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. He appears uncomfortable. His pulse is 95/min. Serum studies show a normal troponin concentration. An ECG shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

options.opb: Coronary artery occlusion due to transient increase in vascular tone
options.opc: Stable atherosclerotic plaque with 85% coronary artery occlusion
options.opd: Disruption of an atherosclerotic plaque with a non-occlusive coronary artery thrombus
options.ope: Atherosclerotic plaque thrombus with complete coronary artery occlusion

analysis: The patient's presentation of retrosternal chest pressure and shortness of breath, especially with minimal improvement at rest, along with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and smoking, is highly concerning for acute coronary syndrome. The absence of ECG abnormalities and normal troponin levels make a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) more likely. Disruption of an atherosclerotic plaque with a non-occlusive coronary artery thrombus is a common cause of NSTEMI.
